newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Saudi Aramco buying 27.5 percent of Petrogal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco buying 27.5 percent of Petrogal.

text.p: Saudi state oil company Saudi Aramco has agreed to buy 27.5 percent of Petrogal, Portugal's biggest oil company, in a deal valued at about $1.3 billion, officials said Thursday.
As part of the deal, Saudi Arabia will significantly increase its oil exports to Petrogal.
"The Portuguese government, Saudi Aramco and Petrocontrol, reached an agreement in principle...for Saudi Aramco...to take a stake in Petrogal-Petroleos de Portugal," the Economy Ministry said.
Petrocontrol, the Portuguese consortium that is the state's current partner in the group, will sell a 17.5 percent share directly to Aramco and the state will sell another 10 percent.

The statement gave no financial details, but a company source said the accord valued Petrogal at between 220 and 230 billion escudos ($1.26 billion and $1.3 billion), with the Aramco stake being worth some 63.25 billion.
The deal will cut Petrocontrol's holding to 27.5 percent, the same as Aramco, while the state will remain the largest stakeholder, at least for the time being.
The deal, which has been under negotiation for more than a year, should be formally concluded by the end of the year, the statement added.
Under the accord, Saudi Aramco will supply Petrogal, which has around half the Portuguese market, with some 40 percent of its annual crude oil needs, a company official said.
He gave no figures, but the company has the capacity to refine 300,000 barrels a day.
As a result, Saudi Arabia will become the country's largest single supplier, overtaking Nigeria which currently has 30 percent of the market.
